the leading-order perturbative predictions are sufficient for the measurement of the color charge factors, and that the leading order perturbation theory is sufficient for the measurement, but not for the prediction of the color charge factor ratio $T_R/C_{F}$.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a leading order measurement of the color charge factors is a valid procedure for experimental analyses.
in the four-jet analysis at LEP, the use of the next-to-leading QCD predictions for the color charge measurements is not recommended.

, in the context of the four-jet event shape distributions, next-to-leading order QCD calculations are not only needed for the precision of the measurements but also for the correct interpretation of the results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to obtain reliable results for the QCD color factors from a fit of the four-jet distributions, the next-to-leading corrections should be included.
the use of the next-to-leading predictions for color charge factors is important for experimental analyses.
